subject: paramedicine
intro: Paramedicine leads into emergency care — the crews who deliver medicine at the roadside, the physicians who take over in the department, and the fire services that answer the call.

roles.title: Paramedics
roles.what: Administer basic and advanced emergency medical care before and during transport — assessing injuries and illness, giving intravenous medication, using ECG equipment and providing advanced life support to the sick and injured.
roles.where: Units 2 to 4 — pre-hospital medications, airway management, patient assessment and ACLS algorithms — are the paramedic skill set; unit 5's medical emergencies and unit 6's haemorrhage control and shock are the everyday caseload.

roles.title: Emergency Medical Technicians
roles.what: Assess injuries and illnesses and administer basic emergency medical care at the scene and en route — stabilising patients, supporting higher-level crews and transporting the injured and sick to medical facilities.
roles.where: Unit 3's primary and secondary survey and vital signs are the EMT's core assessment; unit 1's scene management and wellness, and unit 6's haemorrhage control and shock, cover the interventions delivered before hospital handover.

roles.title: Emergency Medicine Physicians
roles.what: Make immediate medical decisions to prevent death or further disability — recognising, evaluating and stabilising patients and deciding their disposition, often directing the emergency medical staff of an emergency department.
roles.where: Paramedic practice is a recognised route into medicine: unit 4's ECG interpretation and resuscitation, unit 5's stroke, seizure and overdose emergencies and unit 7's paediatric and obstetric cases are the department's intake.

roles.title: Firefighters
roles.what: Control and extinguish fires and respond to emergencies where life, property or the environment is at risk — duties spanning fire prevention, emergency medical service, hazardous materials response, search and rescue and disaster assistance.
roles.where: Unit 1's scene management and unit 7's mass-casualty incident command are the emergency-scene craft; unit 6's trauma and haemorrhage control ground the emergency medical service duty most fire departments deliver.
